title: Enhancing the efficacy of immunotherapy by optimal use of SMAC mimetics
text:
SMAC mimetics can boost antigen presentation in some cancer cells and enhance their response to
immunotherapy, but it is unclear which subset of cancer patients can benefit from SMAC mimetic treatment in
the clinic. This proposal will address the context dependencies of SMAC mimetics’ effects on cancer cells and
identify the optimal combination with immunotherapy. The results from this study can enable effective use of
SMAC mimetics for cancer treatment in the clinic.

title: Human CAR-NK therapy for pathological fibrosis in the heart
text:
Cardiac fibrosis is a leading cause of heart failure, a condition affecting millions worldwide with limited
treatment options targeting the underlying disease process. This research develops a novel, immune-based
therapy using universal CAR-NK cells to selectively eliminate scar-forming cells in the heart without the need for
immunosuppression. If successful, it could provide a safe, scalable treatment to reverse heart damage and
significantly reduce the public health burden of cardiac fibrosis heart failure.

title: Development of Safe and Sustainable Systems of Enhanced Bioremediation of PAH Mixtures
text:
This project aims to develop novel in situ and ex situ biological treatment systems to treat PAH mixtures in
contaminated sediment and soil. We propose to create hydrogel beads that contain immobilized bacteria cultures
extracted from a contaminated site and will apply those hydrogel beads to create permeable reactive biological
barriers for contaminated sediments and to treat soil washing solutions ex situ. We will track transformation
products via high-resolution LC-MS as we treat PAH mixtures.

title: Identification and characterization of molecular subtypes of Alzheimer's disease associated with cognitive function through cross-omics data integration
text:
Clinical and molecular heterogeneity of Alzheimer's disease is increasingly recognized as a major factor
impacting diagnosis, treatment, and most importantly the design and testing of new drugs. Despite the
substantial effort in identifying AD subtypes, there is currently no identified association between pathological
subtypes, cognitive function, and molecular subtypes. The overarching goal of this K25 proposal is to identify
and characterize molecular subtypes of Alzheimer’s disease associated with cognitive function by leveraging
high throughput omics data from different brain regions and cohorts, machine learning, digital deconvolution,
and traditional statistical approaches.

title: Flexible NLP toolkit for automatic curation of outcomes for breast cancer patients
text:
While evidence of long-term clinical outcomes and quality-of-life data for cancer patients is trivial
for treatment planning, manual extraction of data is an extremely challenging task for human
curators and needs hours of manual chart-review. We propose to develop an open-source NLP
toolkit for curating treatment administered (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation, surgery)
and clinical outcome (progression, recurrence) data longitudinally by parsing varying types of
clinical narratives for performing population-wide cancer research. In this study, we will
collaborate with two state-wide cancer registries (Georgia and California) for evaluating our NLP
developments for cancer data curation and obtain a robust performance evaluation across
heterogeneous populations.

title: Exogenic organs in gene edited pigs
text:
Heart disease is common and deadly; the goal and the clinical significance of this proposal are to develop
genetically modified pigs as hosts for the production of a nonhuman primate heart. This nonhuman primate-pig
model will be an important resource for regenerative medicine and will serve as a platform for the future
generation of a humanized heart in a pig. Given the tremendous morbidity and mortality of cardiovascular
diseases in our society, the potential impact of this proposal is tremendous.

title: Broadening the proximity labeling landscape with next generation enzymes, chemistries and probes
text:
Proximity labeling is a technique, that when coupled with proteomics, has vastly enabled molecular discovery in
biological systems. This project focuses on developing novel proximity labeling enzymes, chemical probes, and
chemistries that are highly compatible for tagging proteins in living animals, as well as other cellular biomolecules
like lipids. This development will broaden the applications that can be studied with this method and enable the
exploration of physiological questions that can only be addressed in living organisms.

title: Developing C. elegans as a model to understand tRNA-fragment biogenesis and function
text:
tRNA-fragments (tRFs) are an emerging class of small regulatory RNAs with the ability to
regulate all facets of gene expression. tRFs have been implicated in cancer,
neurogenerative disease, viral infection, fertility, and aging, although little is known about
tRF biogenesis, regulation, and molecular functions throughout the different tissues of an
organism. We are developing the worm C. elegans as a model to address these
questions, thereby providing the first systematic analysis of how tRFs are made and
function throughout an animal to regulate cellular physiology.

title: Anti-tumor immunity and intestinal microbiota are modulated by mitochondrial DNA
text:
Cancer immunotherapy and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) can augment natural immune response
against several tumor types, but not all patients respond, thus it is important to understand the reasons behind
this clinical observation in order to achieve better outcomes. We have observed, in mouse studies, that naturally
occurring differences in the mitochondrial DNA can drastically alter gut microbial composition and immune
responses against melanoma, both mediated by the mitochondrial generation of reactive oxygen species
(mROS) in immune cells. We now propose to determine if this mitochondrial modulation of tumorigenicity is
applicable to other cancers, the immune cell type responsible, the metabolic basis of the mitochondrial-
microbiota interaction, and the importance of immune cell mROS in modulating the efficacy of FMT.

title: Acculturation, Social Context, Loneliness, and the Development of Alcohol Problems in Culturally Representative Individuals
text:
Loneliness is prevalent in the US, and lonely individuals who drink are at elevated risk for problematic alcohol
use. Hispanic individuals represent the largest current international-origin population in the US and a substantial
proportion of the population in the Greater Houston area, providing a strong public health context for examining
acculturation-related mechanisms. Identifying precursors of loneliness in hazardous-drinking individuals from
this population will fill an important gap in explaining the underlying social-cognitive, behavioral, interpersonal,
and cultural mechanisms contributing to loneliness and alcohol problems, and the processes identified in this
research will likely have broad application to additional at-risk populations and social contexts.

title: Integrative role of Rps6kb1 in pathological cardiac remodeling
text:
Heart failure is a leading cause of death worldwide. Pathological cardiac remodeling in response to
hypertension induces the activation of Rps6kb1 in cardiomyocytes, of which precise roles and mechanisms-of-
action are elusive. Experiments laid out here will focus on two novel post-translational modifications of Rps6kb1
in pressure overload-induced cardiomyopathy and heart failure, which may provide new insights for our
understanding of hypertensive heart disease and shed light on novel therapeutic approaches.

title: Role of the Entorhinal Cortical Delta Oscillations in Systems Consolidation
text:
The entorhinal cortex is among the most severely degenerated regions in Alzheimer’s disease; yet, the circuit
mechanism underlying the role of the entorhinal cortex in memory consolidation remains unclear. This project
aims to determine the role of entorhinal cortical oscillations in cortical communication to the hippocampus during
systems consolidation at the circuit and behavioral levels. The outcome of this study would make a significant
advancement in understanding the impairment of memory consolidation in Alzheimer’s disease, which is central
to the development of therapeutic interventions.

title: Aberrant Nuclear Material Properties in Aging Cells
text:
Using new high-throughput tools, we have discovered that nuclear biophysical properties change dramatically
during senescence. We will identify the molecular mechanisms driving these changes and determine how
altered nuclear physical properties causally contribute to transcriptional and splicing dysfunction in senescent
cells. This work will establish perturbations to nuclear physical properties as a fundamental aging mechanism
and identify novel physical intervention strategies for maintaining nuclear homeostasis during aging, with direct
therapeutic implications for age-related diseases including cancer, neurodegeneration, and metabolic
disorders.

title: Prediction of outcomes in diverticulitis using a deep-learning framework
text:
This project seeks to apply artificial intelligence techniques to electronic health records to advance research in
diverticulitis, one of the most common gastrointestinal conditions for emergency department visits and hospital
admissions. We propose to use natural language processing for clinical documentation and deep learning for
imaging to build a prediction model for subsequent external validation to predict recurrence and long-term
complications of diverticulitis. Our project will advance our understanding of factors predictive of diverticulitis
outcomes and contribute to clinical care by generating a risk prediction model for risk stratification that will guide
the appropriate management of the disease.

title: R15: Enhancement of Genome Editing in Hematopoietic Stem Cells by Nucleic Acids Nanoparticles Delivery of CRISPR/CAS System
text:
We propose to develop a nucleic acids nanoparticles technology for the efficient delivery of
genetic materials into hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to guide genome editing. The proposed
research has the potential to advance the treatment of various genetic blood disorders and
related diseases, while also increasing our knowledge of stem cell biology and gene therapy.
The research outcomes are expected to benefit public health by improving patient outcomes
and providing hope for individuals and families affected by genetic disorders, as well as
enhancing Biomedical Sciences education at Rutgers-Camden and the Coriell Institute of
Medical Research.

title: OCT-based functional biomarkers for degenerative diseases of the photoreceptor-RPE-choroid neurovascular unit
text:
In clinical trials of drugs and other therapies to treat blinding diseases of the retina, the FDA’s
recommendation is to use functional assessment, as it is likely to provide earlier indications of their efficacy. In
our lab we have discovered a novel way to measure neural function at the cellular level in the living, human
retina (the optoretinogram), using equipment very similar to that employed in commercial, clinical imaging
systems. The optoretinogram may prove to be faster, less invasive, and more sensitive to neural dysfunction
than existing functional tests. The goal of this grant is to study and improve the technology, and then
demonstrate its sensitivity to disease-related dysfunction in patients with inherited retinal degenerations and
early to intermediate age-related macular degeneration.

title: Establishing Claudin-2 as a Biomarker For Surgical Identification of Colorectal Cancer
text:
This project proposes the initial development of fluorescently labeled antibodies that can specifically
target Cldn2 for improved surgical removal of colon cancer. Cldn2 is a protein that is
highly over-expressed in colon cancer. Therefore, targeting Cldn2 with an imaging agent will highlight
the tumor and its edges to help guided surgeons for more complete CRC resection.

title: Mechanism of cytoskeletal transport and transcription-coupled DNA repair
text:
The directed movement of cargos inside cells by the molecular machines dynein and kinesin is essential for cell
survival. Cell survival is also dependent on the proper repair of DNA damage caused by external factors. This
research will provide fundamental insight into the workings of the molecular machines involved in these two
processes.

title: Peripheral immunity and the aging brain: Studying the relationship of platelet and neutrophil activity with markers of vascular contributions to cognitive decline and dementia
text:
This research aims to elucidate the role of vascular and immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease
(AD) and related dementias (AD/ADRD). By examining the associations between platelet, neutrophil
activity, and proteomic data with advanced imaging measures of cerebrovascular disease and AD
pathology in two human cohorts, this study seeks to identify novel biological mediators and therapeutic
targets. The findings from this multidisciplinary approach have the potential to improve our
understanding of the disease and the identification of novel mediators and targets for intervention,
ultimately benefiting individuals at risk of AD.

title: Maladaptive cortico-amygdalar plasticity after noise-induced hearing loss
text: Hearing loss often leads to distressing symptoms like tinnitus and sound-induced anxiety, significantly impacting people's quality of life. This project investigates how hearing damage affects brain connections between the auditory cortex and the amygdala, potentially explaining why some people develop an oversensitivity to everyday sounds. By understanding these brain changes, we aim to develop better treatments for those suffering from hearing-related emotional distress, ultimately improving their well-being and social interactions.
